### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, when A32 followed A21 within five steps, the gap was most often two positions (about 56 in 100 cases), with about 40 in 100 cases at one position and about 5 in 100 at three positions. In the later window, the gap shifted toward immediate succession: about 58 in 100 cases at one position, about 42 in 100 at two positions, and no three-position cases observed. [LAG001]
- The profile rests on 88 of 200 traces in the earlier window and 109 of 200 in the later window containing the ordered pair within five steps (about 44 vs 55 in 100 traces), so the pair co-occurred somewhat more often in the later window, though this count is the basis of the profile rather than a tested indicator. [LAG001]
- The lag difference is unusual for random re-splits of the pooled data — larger than about 995 of 1,000 reference comparisons — but it is a single item on the positional-lag scale (observed change about 0.06). [LAG001]

### Inference

Support level: Insufficient evidence
The evidence is insufficient to infer a structural change in the process. Only one item qualified across 94 tested units, where about 0.47 items would qualify by chance in an unchanged process, so this single lag shift between A21 and A32 — however unusual for random re-splits — could be a chance sampling difference, and a positional-lag change on one pair cannot by itself establish a structural change. [LAG001]
